simple.meaning: עָב (ʻâb) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an architrave (as shading the pillars).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 7:6. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָב (H5646) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עָב (ʻâb) / H5646 is traced through 1 Kings 7:6, Ezekiel 41:25, Ezekiel 41:26 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He made the porch of pillars. Its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits; with a porch before them, and pillars and a threshold before them.

timeline.evidenceText: He made the porch of pillars. Its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits; with a porch before them, and pillars and a threshold before them.
There were made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls. There was a threshold of wood on the face of the porch outside.
There were closed windows and palm trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch. This is how the side rooms of the house and the thresholds were arranged.

definitions.full: H5646. ab or ob I. עָב , [ עֹב ] noun masculine architectural term, meaning unknown; projecting roof is conjectured (Sm Co Berthol); others landing (Da); AV RV thick beam or plank , RVm threshold ; Benz Kit Toy leave untranslated; in any case a structure of wood; — absolute וְעָב וְעַמֻּדִים 1Kin 7:6 ; apparently construct מֵהַחוּץ הָאוּלָם אֶלמְּֿנֵי עֵץ וְעָב Ezek 41:25 ; plural (si vera lectio) הָעֻבִּים 41:26 . II. עָב see עוּב .
definitions.rootNote: or עֹב ; from an unused root meaning to cover; properly, equivalent to 5645 ; but used only as an architectural term,
